sourceBook: Michael C. Gemignani, Elementary Topology, Second Edition, Addison-Wesley
privateInputPolicy: The supplied PDF, crops, page renders, and side-by-side source comparisons remain local private inputs. No source pages or full PDF are included in these documentation files.

vocabulary.meaning: Coordinates, disk radii, line coefficients, and reciprocal coefficients are mathematical data. Canvas geometry, illustrative contours, colors, hatching, and label placement belong to the style.

reuseVerification: The same diskBoundaryStyle renders distinct substances with radii 1 and 1/2.
One separationStyle handles a point outside a closed set and a pair of disjoint closed sets; both also render with one shared scaled style.
The composed point-set-topology domain can use eulerVennStyleFor without mixing domain-owned descriptors.

verification.typecheck: Bloom declaration emit passed, including subtype metadata and compile-time predicate checks.
verification.rendering: Every canonical substance was built through diagram(), stepped through the optimizer interface, rendered to SVG, rasterized with rsvg-convert, and compared with the source scan on a white background.
verification.geometryPolicy: Coordinate geometry is fixed by mathematical definitions. Separation contours and sample-ball placements are an illustrative style policy; this batch does not require free optimization variables.

retained: two reciprocal branches without artificial endpoint dots
remainingLimits: Irregular contours are hand-tuned cubic curves, not exact traces of scan pixels.
Clean equation lettering differs from the heavier scanned typeface.
A finite drawing of a neighborhood union is illustrative and does not enumerate every ball.
The reciprocal graph is displayed in a finite window; its mathematical substance denotes the entire closed set.
The current reciprocal comparison style supports the positive-coefficient first/third-quadrant case and an x-axis comparison; other affine lines or negative coefficients require another style policy.

sourceRectangleMethod: Graphic and its labels, excluding caption and prose. Rectangles were isolated on inspected 160 dpi page renders, tightened to dark ink with a 2 pixel margin, and divided by the full rendered page dimensions. Coordinates are top-left x,y,width,height in [0,1].

source.context: Example 18; discussion continues on printed page 35 (PDF 41).

mathematics: The boundary points are outside Y although their infimum distances from Y are zero.
D(Z,W)=2 while D(W,Y)+D(Y,Z)=0; this refutes the triangle inequality for set distance.
checks: Strict disk membership excludes both boundary points.
Rendered singleton centers lie exactly one radius from the rendered disk center.
The same style renders a different disk radius without substance shape fields.

visualReview.observations: Axes, disk hatching, singleton dots, labels, leaders, and the origin knockout retained. Hatch orientation was corrected during comparison; label weight remains lighter than the scan.

source.context: Proposition 12 and its proof on printed page 35 (PDF 41).

mathematics: x is outside the closed set F.
U=N(x,D(x,F)/2), and V is the union over y in F of U_y=N(y,D(x,F)/2).
x belongs to U, F is contained in V, and U and V are disjoint. Only one representative U_y is pictured, as in the original.
checks: Substance asserts outside, membership, containment and disjointness with typed signatures.
Sampled rendered F boundary stays outside the displayed neighborhood about x.

visualReview.observations: The one-panel outline, two shaded neighborhoods, x/y points, U_y/F/U labels, dashed segment, and D(x,F) brace retained. White space and label sizing were revised against the crop. The irregular F contour is a hand-tuned approximation.

source.context: Proposition 13 and its proof on printed page 36 (PDF 42).

mathematics: F and F′ are disjoint closed sets.
U is the union of N(y,rho_y) for y in F; V is the union of N(y′,rho′_{y′}) for y′ in F′.
F is contained in U, F′ is contained in V, and U and V are disjoint.
checks: The same separationStyle also renders the Proposition 12 substance.
Rendered cubic outlines were sampled at 40 points per segment: each closed-set boundary is inside its displayed union.
128 samples on each representative circular boundary lie inside its displayed union.
The displayed union boundaries have disjoint horizontal ranges; the representative balls are disjoint.

visualReview.observations: The horizontally arranged irregular sets, hatched open unions, darker representative balls, prime notation, and white point-label knockouts retained. Union and F/F′ contours are approximate cubic curves, with lighter fill than the source.

mathematics: F is the closed zero locus of xy-1; F′ is the closed zero locus of y.
Their intersection is empty since xy=1 and y=0 cannot both hold.
Every finite graph point has positive distance |1/x| from the x-axis, but the infimum over the whole graph is zero as |x| tends to infinity.
checks: Both first- and third-quadrant branches are present.
Every rendered sampled vertex, 161 per branch, satisfies xy=1 to numerical tolerance.
For each tested epsilon>0, choosing x=2/epsilon produces a positive distance smaller than epsilon.
No point at x=0 or artificial endpoint marker is introduced.

visualReview.observations: Axes, origin, F/F′ labels, compact fraction, and both branches retained. The axis location and branch window were revised against the source composition. The analytic polyline is a finite sampling of the exact hyperbola.
